findings.title: Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition breaks organization slug assignment
findings.body: In `createHandler`, `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` was changed to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. This inverts the intended logic in an unrelated file: when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is `false`, newly created organizations will have neither `slug` nor `metadata.requestedSlug` set, and when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is `true`, the slug is assigned immediately before billing completes.

findings.title: Null-dereference on mainHostDestinationCalendar when destinationCalendar is empty or null
findings.body: In `EventManager.create`, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or `[]`. On line 119, `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` is evaluated without optional chaining, which throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` whenever `evt.location === MeetLocationType` and no destination calendar is set.

findings.title: Collective hosts' destination calendars are dropped when organizer has no destinationCalendar
findings.body: At lines 1063-1067, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is defined. At line 1078, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` uses optional chaining on `null` and becomes a no-op, silently dropping all other collective hosts' `destinationCalendar` entries.

findings.title: Broken fallback calendar lookup in GoogleCalendarService updateEvent, deleteEvent, and createEvent patch
findings.body: In `updateEvent` (lines 254-256) and `deleteEvent` (lines 315-317), the fallback branch of `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`null`, `undefined`, or `""`), so `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` can never match a destination calendar and `selectedCalendar` evaluates to `undefined`. Additionally, in `createEvent`, `selectedCalendar` is now `string | undefined` (`"primary"` is only applied inline at line 154), so `calendar.events.patch` at line 168 passes `calendarId: undefined` instead of `"primary"` when updating the event with a Hangout link.

findings.title: Non-Google calendar services always use the primary host's destinationCalendar for all hosts
findings.body: `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` (line 73), `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` and `createAttendees` (`packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` lines 128, 164), and `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` (`packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` line 156) all destructure `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` instead of matching by `credentialId`. In a collective booking, when `createEvent` runs for any host other than the first, these services use the first host's `externalId` (which belongs to another user and potentially a different calendar provider), causing event creation on Office 365, Lark, and CalDAV calendars to fail or be skipped for additional hosts.

findings.title: Recurring booking cancellation only uses organizer credentials and first calendar reference
findings.body: When cancelling all remaining instances of a recurring booking (`allRemainingBookings`), lines 449-461 iterate over `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` (only the primary organizer's credentials, ignoring `calendarCredential` fetched from the database for other collective hosts) and look up `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))` (only the first calendar reference). Because this block is also nested inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`, it repeats the organizer's deletions for each reference while never deleting the recurring events from other collective hosts' calendars.

findings.title: Unchecked undefined credential passed to updateEvent in updateAllCalendarEvents
findings.body: In `updateAllCalendarEvents` (lines 511-542), if `reference.credentialId` is not found in `this.calendarCredentials` and the database lookup either returns `null` or a credential without `app?.slug`, `credential` remains `undefined`. Unlike `createAllCalendarEvents` (line 369), line 542 calls `updateEvent(credential, ...)` without checking `if (credential)`, which causes `CalendarManager.updateEvent` to throw when accessing `credential.appName`.
